{\scriptsize\textit{Notes:} $\hat\alpha$ in percent per month. North America, vintages up to 2010: Buyout 25 vintages; VC 27, of which the 23 with at least two funds enter $U_{v,H}$. $U_{v,H}$: the cross-fund pair-product criterion with equal vintage weights ($q_v=1$); without shared vintage effects and with the expected pricing error zero given the benchmark path, it targets the true parameter at every horizon, $H=0$ included. L2: squared loss on vintage portfolios (DLP12 at $H=0$), whose target is tilted by within-vintage fund noise and moves with $H$. SE: Bartlett sandwich over vintage years, $S=\lceil1.3\sqrt V\rceil$. Markers on $U_{v,H}$: two-sided fixed-$b$ $p$-values of a test of zero, $^{*}$\,$p<0.05$, $^{**}$\,$p<0.01$, $^{***}$\,$p<0.001$. $^{\dagger}$: estimate on a bound of the admissible domain ($\beta\in[-1,4]$, $\alpha\in[-2\%,2\%]$ per month, gross benchmark return at least 0.08), no SE. In VC the estimate at $H=0$ is on the upper bound of $\alpha$ under both criteria because the criterion keeps falling in $\alpha$; that comes from the 1993--1997 vintages as a group, and without them $\hat\alpha$ is negative at every horizon (Table~\ref{tab:vc_without_1993_1997}). The horizon then imposes a minimum in $\alpha$ without identifying it.}
